_help: Known physics mistakes. whatif.py check FAILs when script, captions or climax match a pattern (case-insensitive regex). Add every new mistake a review finds: pattern + why + fix.

myths.why: rock, sand or tar only glow above about 500 °C; sunlight on Earth heats the ground to at most about 70–80 °C.
myths.fix: say it is too hot to touch, or that the air shimmers above it.

myths.why: about 1 361 W/m² is the sunlight ABOVE the atmosphere; at the ground it is at most about 1 000 W/m² (sun overhead, clear sky).
myths.fix: use about 1 000 W per square metre at the ground.

myths.pattern: \bsea\b[^.]{0,20}\b(pulls|draws|drains|runs)\s+(back|away)\b[^.]{0,30}\b(as far as|out of sight|to the horizon)\b
myths.why: only a tsunami pulls the sea back that far; tides or a missing Moon change the water level by centimetres to a few metres.
myths.fix: give the real change in metres, or make it a tsunami story.

myths.why: there is no sound in a vacuum (space, the Moon): no air carries it.
myths.fix: show it silently, or let the sound travel through the ground or a suit/helmet.

myths.why: in orbit gravity is still about 90 %; astronauts float because they are falling around the Earth.
myths.fix: say they are falling around the Earth, or 'weightless'.

myths.why: a body in a vacuum does not freeze instantly; vacuum insulates and heat leaves slowly by radiation.
myths.fix: talk about the lack of air (unconscious in about 15 s), not instant freezing.

myths.why: a body does not explode in a vacuum; skin holds it together, it swells a little.
myths.fix: describe swelling and the lack of air instead.

myths.why: the far side of the Moon gets as much sunlight as the near side; it is only hidden from us.
seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance; Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.
the Great Wall is too narrow to see with the naked eye from orbit, and certainly not from the Moon.
all water vapour in the atmosphere together is only about 25 mm of rain over the whole Earth.
myths.fix: endless rain must be fed by evaporation from the sea or brought by a river from a big area.

myths.pattern: \bcoolest hour\b[^.]{0,80}\b(sun (stands|stood|stays) still|never moves)\b|\b(sun (stands|stood|stays) still|never moves)\b[^.]{0,80}\bcoolest hour\b
myths.why: if the Sun stands still in the sky, every hour is the same: there is no coolest hour.
myths.fix: count days of sun and the rising temperature until it levels off.
